name: Demas
overview: Demas is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament who is noted for sending greetings through the Apostle Paul to the believers in Colossae. Beyond this act of communication, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or additional background information. His mention highlights his connection to the early Christian community and to Paul.
namesAndTitles: The name Demas appears as a proper name in the Scriptures, specifically in Colossians 4:14. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Demas beyond his association with Paul as indicated by his sending of greetings. No other relational ties are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Demas is significant primarily for his association with the Apostle Paul, as he is mentioned as one who sends greetings through Paul to the church in Colossae. This brief mention situates Demas within the network of early Christian workers and believers who supported the ministry of the apostles. His presence in the epistle underscores the communal and relational nature of the early church.
